questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Why is the eulachon fish also known as the “candlefish”?
A. Because it glows like a candle
B. Because it can be lighted up as a candle
C. Because its scales resemble candle wax
Answer: B. The eulachon fish has such a high oil content that it can be dried, fitted with a wick, and lighted up as a candle.
questions.en: Which small, very oily Pacific smelt is called the 'candlefish' because, dried and strung on a wick, it can be burned as a candle?
questions.de: Welcher kleine, sehr fettreiche Stint des Pazifiks wird „Kerzenfisch“ genannt, weil er getrocknet und mit einem Docht versehen wie eine Kerze brennt?

timeline.labelEn: John Richardson first describes the eulachon (candlefish) scientifically, as Salmo pacificus
timeline.labelDe: John Richardson beschreibt den Eulachon (Kerzenfisch) erstmals wissenschaftlich, als Salmo pacificus

questions.notes: Card asks why it is called candlefish (oil content, burns on a wick); reworked to ask the fish from that fact, so the answer is a single name.

questions.cardText:
[Engineering and Invention] What are modern solar panels usually made from?
A. Graphite
B. Silicon
C. Nickel
Answer: B. Silicon is a semiconductor material that can efficiently convert sunlight into electricity. Silicon solar cells work by absorbing photons from sunlight, which then knock electrons loose from the silicon atoms. These free electrons flow through the material to produce an electric current, which can be harnessed for power.
questions.en: From which semiconductor material are almost all commercial solar cells in today's solar panels made?
questions.de: Aus welchem Halbleitermaterial bestehen fast alle kommerziellen Solarzellen heutiger Solarmodule?

timeline.labelEn: Bell Labs demonstrates the first practical silicon solar cell
timeline.labelDe: Die Bell Labs führen die erste praxistaugliche Silizium-Solarzelle vor

questions.notes: Crystalline silicon has about a 95% market share of commercial PV cells.
